title: Dust Jacket Cover the Wrong Size? IngramSpark & Barnes & Noble Press Jacket Sizes | SparkPrep
h1: How to fix a hardcover dust jacket that's the wrong size
description: A dust jacket needs flaps, folds and panels bigger than the trim. See IngramSpark's and B&N Press's own jacket sizes and fix your file.
lead: A dust jacket is the paper cover that wraps around a hardcover and tucks inside with flaps. It's much wider than any other cover.
error: Dust jacket file does not match the jacket template size
errorNote: Paraphrased. Each printer words this a little differently.
why:
A dust jacket has seven parts from left to right: back flap, fold, back panel, spine, front panel, fold, front flap. Each flap is 3.25" and each fold is 0.25", plus 0.125" bleed around the outside.

The panels are bigger than your trim because the jacket covers the boards. For a 6" x 9" book:

  • IngramSpark: each panel is the trim + 0.4375" wide and + 0.25" tall. Their own template for a 0.313" spine is 20.438" x 9.5".
  • Barnes & Noble Press: same layout, but each panel is about trim + 0.4445" wide. Their own template for a 0.31" spine is 20.451" x 9.5".

Amazon KDP and Lulu don't offer a dust jacket binding at all, so there is no jacket file to make for them.
manual: Download your printer's own dust jacket template for your exact trim size, page count and paper.
Set your cover document to the template's full size.
Line up the back flap, back panel, spine, front panel and front flap with the template, and keep text off the 0.25" folds.
Hide the template layer, flatten, and export as PDF/X-1a:2001.
Re-upload it to your printer and wait for the file review again. If it fails, you start over.
quickfix: SparkPrep checks your dust jacket against your printer's own jacket size, flaps and folds, and shows exactly what's off.

cta.text: SparkPrep checks your jacket against IngramSpark's or B&N Press's own jacket numbers (they differ) and flags text sitting on the folds.

faq.q: How wide are dust jacket flaps?
faq.a: 3.25" each at IngramSpark and Barnes & Noble Press, with a 0.25" fold between each flap and its panel.

faq.q: Can I print a dust jacket through KDP?
faq.a: No. KDP's hardcover is case laminate only, so it has no dust jacket option.
